reviews.review: cant stop playing it. 50 hours in and still loving it
simple rpg game with resource and level upgrades. Very addictive and quite hard.

Better that most extraction shooters - plus, it doesn't feel like you have to treat the game as a second job to build loadouts.

Edit: Having completed the game, and having done everything aside from the latest update, I can safely say that after just under 100 hours for the first playthrough, the game is really really solid. I've now added a dozen mods, and somehow the game is even better! Although I wouldn't suggest that you add mods on your first way through, there's plenty of QoL mods, gameplay altering mods, and by the looks of things some real silly/funny stuff on the workshop as well.
After almost 100 hours all I can say is Duck Around And Find Out!

I was enjoying it for a bit but it feels like half the things that kill me are things I really have no chance to stop. Like I had a pretty rough death, but it felt like something where I could just get my gear back and turn it around. 

Then I loaded back into the zone and was attacked by a half dozen dogs less than five seconds, died, and lost my chance to retrieve my good gear. That's when I decided I'm not going to play a game that's just going to piss me other round.

Escape from Duckov is a casual top-down PVE extraction shooter. The premise is straightforward: you play as an anthropomorphic duck whose sole goal is to escape the harsh world of "Duckov."

[b]The Short Answer: Is It Worth Buying?[/b]
If you love PVE Tarkov and top-down shooters—YES, absolutely YES.

[b]Playtime[/b] 7/10
It took me 50 hours to complete all the quests (except for fishing), but it was a blast the entire time. It only started feeling tedious right at the very end because of a specific end-game area that requires specialized high-tier gear just to enter.

[b]Story[/b] 2/10
Escape from Duckov... playing as a duck.

[b]Music[/b] 6/10
Vibes like a cheerful farm simulator soundtrack, but surprisingly catchier and more fun.

[b]Graphics[/b] 4/10
Casual, lighthearted style.

[b]Mechanics[/b] 6/10
The core top-down shooter mechanics feel incredibly solid. The shooting, movement, dodging, and looting loops are exceptionally smooth and satisfying. Modifying weapons is present, though not nearly as deep or complex as in Tarkov.
Without mods, the base economy feels very tedious and heavily tuned toward a constant cash drain—essentially mimicking Tarkov without a Flea Market. Standard enemy ducks and "PMC" equivalents feel fairly weak, especially past the early game. However, the bosses are a major highlight: they are varied, possess distinct combat behaviors, and directly parody Tarkov's iconic bosses (Killa, Tagilla, Shturman, and even the guy with the baton). The game also features unique original bosses.
Bitcoin mining is present, but it feels heavily nerfed and unrewarding—a single Bitcoin fetches around 7k, which is barely worth two basic AKS rifles. While there appears to be a wide variety of weapons on paper, you'll realistically end up using the same 3–4 meta guns for most of your runs. On the bright side, you get a clear map with active location markers, though the overall UI leaves a bit to be desired.

[b]Personal Take[/b] 
It’s a fantastic little game, especially considering it has day-one Steam Workshop mod support. The main downside with the modding scene right now is that a lot of great mods are Chinese-only with no translations available yet.
The overall gameplay speed feels as fast-paced and snappy as a good mobile shooter. Out of the box, the base game lacks enough vanity loot and high-value chase items; picking up nuts and bolts is fun at first, but you quickly crave rarer, expensive drops. Without workshop mods, the economy feels a bit dry.

[b]Overall Score:[/b] 74/100 (Note: This score accounts for playing with Steam Workshop mods installed; without mods, subtract about 4–5 points).
